title: How To Choose EDI Software: A Guide for New Suppliers
summary: Learn how to choose EDI software with clear EDI provider comparison criteria, from retailer coverage to ASN accuracy, built for new retail suppliers.
body_markdown:
In this article, learn about:


-


How to choose EDI software when a retailer sets a compliance deadline


-


The four types of EDI providers and the supplier each one fits


-


EDI provider comparison criteria and the questions to ask vendors


____________________________________________________________________________________
Choosing the right[electronic data interchange (EDI)](https://www.spscommerce.com/what-is-edi/) software starts with understanding your business needs including order volume, internal resources, and retailer requirements.


When comparing EDI providers, suppliers should consider five key factors:


-


**Retailer coverage** : Does the provider support your current retail partners and make it easy to connect with new ones?


-


**ASN accuracy** : Can the provider help ensure[advance ship notices (ASNs)](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/edi-856-ship-notice-manifest?utm_source=chatgpt.com) meet retailer requirements and accurately reflect shipment details?


-


**Ongoing mapping maintenance** : Does the provider manage EDI mapping updates as retailer requirements change?


-


**System integration** : Can the solution connect with your existing ERP, accounting, warehouse, or inventory management systems?


-


**Scalable pricing** : Is the pricing structure clear, predictable, and affordable as transaction volumes and trading relationships grow?


After months of pitches, samples, and negotiations, a major retailer has agreed to carry your product. The routing guide arrives next, with a deadline to start exchanging purchase orders (POs,[EDI 850](https://spscommerce.com/edi-document/edi-850-purchase-order) ), invoices ([EDI 810](https://www.spscommerce.com/edi-document/edi-810-electronic-invoice/) ), and ASNs (EDI 856) electronically. Under that pressure, it’s tempting to treat the choice as a procurement task and choose the lowest upfront price that clears the specifications for the 850, 856, and 810.


Buying EDI is a multi-year operational commitment, though. The provider determines whether your team keys each EDI 850 into the order system by hand, how fast you can add a second retailer, and how many chargebacks reach your remittance.


## Why Does Your EDI Provider Matter Beyond the Price?


The provider matters because most EDI costs appear after the contract is signed, as manual work, scaling delays, and retailer penalties. The most expensive EDI solution is the one that is cheap on day one but fails on day 100.


Walmart’s[On Time, In Full (OTIF)](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/walmart-otif-fundamentals) program shows how those penalties work. Suppliers that miss the target are[fined 3% of the cost of goods](https://www.8thandwalton.com/blog/walmart-otif) on the cases that fall short.


Walmart's[Supplier Quality Excellence Program (SQEP)](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/sqep-fines-explained) runs alongside OTIF. It covers purchase order accuracy, labeling, and ASN quality, with[SQEP penalties](https://beancount.io/blog/2026/10/14/walmart-otif-chargebacks-on-time-in-full-targets-fines-dispute-guide) of $200 per defective PO plus $1 per impacted case.


An inaccurate ASN can therefore trigger SQEP fees on top of the 3% OTIF fine. Avoiding these costs requires an EDI provider that double-checks data before it reaches the retailer.


## Which Type of EDI Provider Fits Your Business?


The right type depends on transaction volume, internal IT resources, and the number of retailers a supplier plans to add.


**Provider Type**


**Best For**


**Trade-Off**


Full-service managed provider


High volume, limited internal IT, fast growth across several big-box retailers


Higher service fee, in exchange for less manual work and lower chargeback risk


Software as a service (SaaS) self-service portal


Very low volume or a narrow retailer mix


The supplier’s team maintains compliance and troubleshoots errors


[Integration software delivered as a service (iPaaS)](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/ipaas-for-edi-workflows-the-pros-and-cons-of-local-versus-cloud-based-tools) with an EDI module


Tech-heavy teams that want one system for every integration


Modules can lack the retailer-specific depth that grocery and big-box routing guides require


In-house build


Rarely a fit


Every retailer specification change requires new mapping, which drains engineering time


## What Are the Key EDI Provider Comparison Criteria?


Five criteria separate providers that protect margins from providers that only transmit documents. Suppliers can score each vendor against them during a demo:


-


**Retailer coverage and mapping breadth:** A provider already connected to the retailer, such as[KeHE](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/how-to-manage-orders-at-kehe) or[UNFI](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/unfi-supplier-compliance-guide) for grocery, goes live faster than one building the connection new. Suppliers should ask how many trading partner requirements it has mapped.


-


**ASN accuracy and chargeback prevention:** Retailers check each ASN (EDI 856) against the shipment. Built-in validation rules should catch a missing pallet ID or a wrong item count before the retailer sees it.


-


**Mapping update maintenance:** Retailers change specifications often. Some providers apply updates automatically for every customer, and others bill a professional services project each time a data field changes.


-


**Integration with business systems:** Direct integration removes manual data entry as volume grows. It can link EDI to an enterprise resource planning (ERP) system, warehouse management system (WMS), or accounting software like Shopify, QuickBooks, or NetSuite.


-


**Pricing at scale:** A quote at three times current volume shows whether costs stay predictable as the supplier adds retailers.


A demo built around the retailer’s actual ASN requirements shows how validation rules handle real data, which a generic example doesn’t.


## What Questions Should You Ask EDI Vendors?


These direct questions get past the marketing polish during an evaluation:


-


How many active connections do you currently maintain with \[retailer name\]?


-


What is your average implementation timeline for a supplier with my specific profile?


-


How do you handle mapping updates when a retailer changes its technical specifications?


-


Do you offer built-in validation to catch errors before a document is sent?


-


What does your support model look like when a shipment is stuck on a Friday afternoon?


-


Can you show me how your pricing scales as my transaction volume triples?


### What Are the Red Flags in an EDI Vendor?


Suppliers should be wary of a provider that shows any of these walk-away signals.


-


Vague answers about implementation timelines


-


Mapping updates billed as professional services hours


-


Pricing that scales punitively with transaction volume, which penalizes growth


-


No clear support escalation path


-


No visibility into how the provider prevents chargebacks


## How Do You Calculate the Total Cost of EDI Software?


Compare[total cost of ownership (TCO)](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/total-cost-of-ownership-in-software-procurement) over three to five years rather than the upfront price. A TCO calculation adds internal labor, professional services fees for each new retailer, and the chargebacks a provider failed to catch, such as a 3% OTIF fine.


Grillo’s Pickles saved[about 50 hours of manual work](https://www.casestudies.com/company/sps-commerce/case-study/grillos-pickles-cuts-60-hours-of-weekly-manual-work-and-grows-4x-with-sps-commerce) each week after moving to automated order processing. Then, the company grew from 10 to more than 46 trading partners without ever adding customer service staff.


A decision made under deadline pressure is also costly to reverse. Switching providers later means remapping and retesting every retailer connection.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### How do I choose EDI software for my first retailer?


Start with the retailer’s routing guide, which lists the required documents, usually the EDI 850 purchase order, EDI 856 ASN, and EDI 810 invoice. Then pick a provider that already connects to that retailer and checks ASNs before sending them.


### What is the difference between SaaS and managed EDI?


With SaaS, the supplier’s team maintains compliance and fixes errors. A managed provider handles mapping updates and retailer communication for a higher fee.


### What should an EDI provider comparison include?


An EDI provider comparison should score each vendor on retailer coverage, ASN validation, mapping updates, integration, and pricing at triple volume.


### How long does it take to set up EDI?


Timelines depend on the provider and the retailer’s testing requirements. A provider with an existing connection to the retailer can go live faster.


### Should a new supplier build EDI in-house?


In-house builds are rarely a fit, because every retailer specification change requires new mapping and pulls engineers away from other projects.
